# 🔍 BEFORE ANY DEPLOYMENT — Safety Checks (Important!)

Before running **ANY delete, commit, or push**, always check:

## ✅ 1. Verify you are inside the correct project folder

```bash
pwd
ls -al
```

You must see your **website files** (index.qmd, docs/, styles.css, etc.). If you see things like **Documents, Desktop, AppData**, STOP — wrong folder.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ✅ 2. Check what is currently in GitHub (online)

Open:

```         
https://github.com/HabtamuBizuayehu/habtamubizuayehu.github.io
```

Confirm:

-   Which files exist
-   Whether Github Pages is building
-   Whether it looks empty
-   Whether old files still appear

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ✅ 3. Check git status

``` bash
git status
```

Look for:

-   **Untracked files**
-   **Modified files**
-   **Deleted but unstaged** files
-   Whether the repo is clean

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ✅ 4. Check last commit history (optional)

``` bash
git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Standard Deployment (NO Large Files)


We first need to create the repository in GitHub and then follow the steps below to complete pushing the website files.

---

 ✅ Complete and Clean Push Procedure

This procedure deploys the website **from scratch** and works even if previous pushes failed or the repository was corrupted.

 Deployment details

**Local project folder**

```
C:\Users\User\Desktop\Materials_ Course and proposals\Github\Website profile Mod 2
```

**GitHub repository**

```
https://github.com/HabtamuBizuayehu/habtamubizuayehu.github.io
```

---

 Step 1 — Navigate to the project folder

Open **Git Bash** and run:

```bash
cd "/c/Users/User/Desktop/Materials_ Course and proposals/Github/Website profile Mod 2"
```

Verify the files:

```bash
ls
```

You should see `.qmd` files, `_freeze`, `Post_Blog`, and other project folders.

---

 Step 2 — Create a fresh `.gitignore`

```bash
nano .gitignore
```

Paste the following:

```text
*.Rhistory
*.RData
*.Rproj.user
.Rproj.user/
.Rhistory
.RData
.DS_Store
.Ruserdata
__pycache__/
*.py[cod]
*.ipynb_checkpoints
```

Save using:
- `Ctrl + O`, then `Enter`
- `Ctrl + X`

---

 Step 3 — Remove any previous Git data

This ensures no leftover metadata or large files remain.

```bash
rm -rf .git
```

Verify:

```bash
ls -a
```

The `.git` directory should no longer appear.

---

 Step 4 — Initialise a new Git repository

```bash
git init
```

Verify:

```bash
ls -a
```

You should now see the `.git/` directory.

---

 Step 5 — Add all files

Ensure no individual file exceeds **100 MB**, then run:

```bash
git add -A
```

Check staged files:

```bash
git status
```

You should see multiple files ready to commit.

---

 Step 6 — Commit the website

```bash
git commit -m "Initial upload of website (fresh repository)"
```

---

 Step 7 — Link the repository to GitHub

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/HabtamuBizuayehu/habtamubizuayehu.github.io
git branch -M main
```

Verify:

```bash
git remote -v
```

Expected output:

```text
origin  https://github.com/HabtamuBizuayehu/habtamubizuayehu.github.io (fetch)
origin  https://github.com/HabtamuBizuayehu/habtamubizuayehu.github.io (push)
```

---

 Step 8 — Push the entire website

```bash
git push -u origin main --force
```

This will:
- Overwrite GitHub with a fresh repository
- Avoid previous large-file conflicts
- Upload all content, including `_site/`, `docs/`, `_freeze/`, and `Post_Blog/`

---

 ✅ Completion

The website will be available at:

- https://habtamuBizuayehu.github.io

If a custom domain is configured, it will also be available at:

- https://habtamubizuayehu.com


# 2. Replace the ENTIRE Website (Full Rebuild)

Use this when:

-   Website is corrupted
-   Bad files exist online
-   Wrong structure
-   You want a full clean rebuild

## ⚠️ SAFETY CHECK FIRST

### Step A — Check what is in the online repo

Go to the GitHub repo and confirm:

-   Which files exist
-   Whether there is anything to keep (README, LICENSE, CNAME)

### Step B — Make a backup of local site (optional)

Copy the entire folder to a backup:

```         
Website profile Mod 2 BACKUP/
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2.1 Clone fresh (recommended)

``` bash
cd C:/Users/User
git clone https://github.com/HabtamuBizuayehu/habtamubizuayehu.github.io
cd habtamubizuayehu.github.io
pwd
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2.2 Remove ALL tracked files (wipe clean)

``` bash
git rm -r .
git add -A
git commit -m "Remove all website files for full rebuild"
git push origin main
```

GitHub repo becomes **empty**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2.3 Copy NEW website files

### Option A — Manual copy

Copy all new files from:

```         
Website profile Mod 2/
```

to:

```         
C:\Users\User\habtamubizuayehu.github.io
```

### Option B — Build then push

``` bash
quarto render
git add .
git commit -m "Upload clean rebuilt website"
git push origin main
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. Add OR Delete Selected Files Only (Partial Updates)

Use this for small changes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.1 Add or update a file

``` bash
git add styles.css
git commit -m "Update styles.css"
git push
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.2 Delete a file

⚠️ SAFETY CHECK:

-   Ensure file exists locally using `ls`
-   Ensure file exists online (optional)

Then delete:

``` bash
git rm old_photo.jpg
git commit -m "Remove old photo"
git push
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4. GitHub Large File Limits (100MB)

GitHub blocks any file over:

```         
100 MB
```

You have two options:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4.1 OPTION A — Exclude Large File (recommended)

### Step 1 — Add to `.gitignore`

```         
Post_Blog/SQL_Database_Guide/SQL_Data_Manipulation
```

### Step 2 — Remove from repo

``` bash
git rm --cached "Post_Blog/SQL_Database_Guide/SQL_Data_Manipulation"
git add .
git commit -m "Remove large file and ignore it"
git push
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 4.2 OPTION B — Use Git LFS (Large File Storage)

⚠ GitHub Pages **cannot serve LFS files** ⚠ Large files stored via LFS do NOT appear on your website

Use only when storing data for repository use.

### Steps:

``` bash
git lfs install
git lfs track "Post_Blog/SQL_Database_Guide/*"
git add .gitattributes
git add .
git commit -m "Track large files with LFS"
git push
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 5. GitHub Error: File \>100MB (Even After Deleting)

This happens because the large file exists in **history**, not in the working folder.

The fix = rewrite history.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 5.1 Remove file from ALL HISTORY (advanced)

``` bash
git filter-repo --force --path "Post_Blog/SQL_Database_Guide/SQL_Data_Manipulation" --invert-paths
```

This:

-   Removes file from all commits
-   Shrinks repo
-   Removes remote origin (normal)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 5.2 Reconnect to remote repo

``` bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/HabtamuBizuayehu/habtamubizuayehu.github.io
git remote -v
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 5.3 Commit and push cleaned history

``` bash
git add .
git commit -m "Clean history and remove large file"
git push origin main --force
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 6. GitHub Pages Publishing

Settings → Pages:

-   **Branch:** main
-   **Folder:** /docs
-   **HTTPS:** enabled once certificate is ready
-   **Custom domain:** habtamubizuayehu.com

DNS/SSL may take **10–30 minutes**.

# 7. **GitHub Pages Custom Domain Setup & Verification Guide**
Fixing the 'Domain Already Taken' Error on Namecheap

## 1. 🛑 Problem Scenario & Solution Overview

This guide addresses how to successfully configure a custom domain (e.g., `habtamubizuayehu.com`) from Namecheap for GitHub Pages, focusing on the common **"The custom domain is already taken"** error.

This error requires **Account-Level Verification** to prove ownership and 'release' the domain before you can configure the traffic-directing records.

| Phase | Goal | Records Involved | Location |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Phase A** | **Traffic Configuration & Cleanup** | `A Records`, `AAAA Record` | Namecheap Advanced DNS |
| **Phase B** | **Domain Verification & Release** | `TXT Record` | GitHub Settings $\rightarrow$ Namecheap Advanced DNS $\rightarrow$ GitHub Settings |
| **Phase C** | **Final Setup** | N/A | GitHub Repository Pages Settings |

---

## 2. 🗺️ Phase A: Namecheap DNS Configuration & Cleanup

The first step is to ensure your domain is set to use Namecheap's default nameservers and to configure the records that direct traffic to GitHub.

**Accessing Namecheap Advanced DNS Settings**

**Crucial Prerequisite:** Your domain must be set to use **Namecheap BasicDNS, PremiumDNS, or FreeDNS** to manage host records in the *Advanced DNS* tab. If it uses custom nameservers, you must make these changes with your external hosting provider.

1.  **Log In:** Sign into your Namecheap account.
2.  **Domain List:** From the sidebar menu, click **Domain List**.
3.  **Manage:** Find your domain (`yourdomain.com`) and click the **Manage** button next to it.
4.  **Nameservers Check:** On the *Domain* tab, locate the **Nameservers** section. Ensure the option selected is one of Namecheap's DNS services (e.g., **Namecheap BasicDNS**).
5.  **Advanced DNS Tab:** Click the **Advanced DNS** tab at the top of the page. You will find the **Host Records** section here.

**2.2. Delete Conflicting Records**

In the **Host Records** section, remove any records that interfere with GitHub Pages hosting. Click the **trash icon** on the right side of the record to delete it.

| Record Type | Host | Value (Example) | Action | Reason |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AAAA Record` | `@` | `2606:c0:8003::153` | **DELETE** | Conflicts with GitHub's current IPv4-focused setup. |
| `TXT Record` | `_github-pages-...` | (Old Code) | **DELETE** | Old or incorrect verification challenge. |

**2.3. Configure Required A Records**

Add the following four **A Records** to point the root domain (`@` or `habtamubizuayehu.com`) to GitHub's current load balancer IP addresses.

1.  Click **ADD NEW RECORD**.
2.  Select **A Record** for the *Type*.

| Type | Host | Value | Note |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `A Record` | `@` | `185.199.108.153` | Point root domain to GitHub |
| `A Record` | `@` | `185.199.109.153` | Point root domain to GitHub |
| `A Record` | `@` | `185.199.110.153` | Point root domain to GitHub |
| `A Record` | `@` | `185.199.111.153` | Point root domain to GitHub |

**2.4. Verify CNAME Record (for `www`)**

Ensure the CNAME record is configured to point the `www` subdomain to the root domain.

| Type | Host | Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `CNAME Record` | `www` | `yourdomain.com.` (or `habtamubizuayehu.com.`) |

---

## 3. 🔑 Phase B: GitHub Account-Level Verification & Release

This critical step fixes the "domain is already taken" error by proving ownership at the account level.

** 3.1. Generate the Unique Verification Code (GitHub)**

1.  **Log in to GitHub.**
2.  Go to your **Profile Settings** (click your avatar) $\rightarrow$ **Settings**.
3.  In the left sidebar, under "Code, planning, and automation," click **Pages**.
4.  If the domain is listed as **Unverified**, click the three dots (`...`) next to it and select **"View verification instructions."**
5.  **Copy the entire, unique TXT Record Value** provided by GitHub.

    > *Example Code Format:* `github-pages-verify=a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8...` **(This code is unique to you.)**

**3.2. Add the Correct TXT Record (Namecheap)**

1.  Return to your **Namecheap Advanced DNS** $\rightarrow$ **Host Records**.
2.  Click **ADD NEW RECORD**.

| Type | Host | Value | Note |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TXT Record` | `@` | *(Paste the unique code copied in Step 3.1)* | This must match GitHub's code exactly. |

**3.3. Verify Domain and Release**

1.  Wait **5-15 minutes** for the TXT record to propagate.
2.  Return to your **GitHub Settings** $\rightarrow$ **Pages**.
3.  Click the **Verify** button next to `yourdomain.com`.
4.  Once verification is successful, the domain is released and available for your repository.

---

## 4. ✅ Phase C: Final Repository Configuration

1.  Go to your specific **project repository** on GitHub (e.g., `github.com/yourusername/yourrepo`).
2.  Go to **Settings** $\rightarrow$ **Pages**.
3.  Under *Custom domain*, enter: `habtamubizuayehu.com`
4.  Click **Save**.

The domain should now save without the error. Allow **12-48 hours** for all DNS changes and SSL certificate provisioning to fully take effect across the internet.


# **8. GitHub Pages Custom Domain Locked and did not work After Repo Deletion**


## What happened 

1. A repository was initially **created**
2. The custom domain **`habtamubizuayehu.com`** was **attached** to that repository
3. The repository was later **deleted**
4. GitHub **did not release the associated domain lock**
5. When attempting to reuse the domain, GitHub now reports:

> **“The custom domain is already taken”**

This occurs **despite the following being true**:

- ✅ The domain is owned by the user  
- ✅ DNS records are correctly configured  
- ✅ A valid TXT verification record exists  

As a result, the domain remains **locked within GitHub’s internal Pages domain registry**.

This issue is **not user error** and **not related to DNS configuration**.

---

 ✅ Important clarification (to avoid unnecessary DNS troubleshooting)

At this stage:

- ❌ Changing Namecheap DNS settings will **not** resolve the issue  
- ❌ Waiting for DNS propagation will **not** resolve the issue  
- ❌ Recreating repositories will **not** resolve the issue  

✅ **Only one action will resolve this**

---

## Fix — Release the domain at the account level

GitHub Pages custom domains are locked **globally at the account level**, even if the original repository has been deleted.

---

Step 1 — Open GitHub Pages domain management (account level)

Open the following link (not a repository settings page):

👉 <https://github.com/settings/pages/domains>

(Ensure you are logged into the correct GitHub account.)

---

Step 2 — What you will likely see

One of the following scenarios will apply:

Case A — Domain listed as “Not verified” or “In use”

```

habtamubizuayehu.com

```

➡️ Select **Verify**, or  
➡️ Select **Remove / Release**

---

 Case B — Domain listed but locked

The domain is visible but cannot be reused.

➡️ Select **Remove domain**

*(This action only releases the domain and does not affect DNS records or repository content.)*

---

 Case C — Domain not listed at all

This can occur when a repository has been deleted.

➡️ In this case, **GitHub Support intervention is required** (usually resolved quickly).

---

Step 3 — Add the domain again to the new repository

After the domain is released or verified:

1. Navigate to  
   **Repository → Settings → Pages**
2. Enter:


habtamubizuayehu.com

3. Select **Save**

✅ The domain should now be accepted immediately.

---

 If the domain is not visible at `/settings/pages/domains`

This indicates the domain is **orphan-locked** (left behind after repository deletion).

Final resolution (guaranteed)

Submit a GitHub Support request:

👉 <https://support.github.com/contact>

**Recommended selections:**

- Product: **GitHub Pages**  
- Issue: **Custom domain**

**Description (copy and paste exactly):**

I previously attached the custom domain habtamubizuayehu.com to a GitHub Pages repository.
That repository was deleted, and the domain was never released.
I now cannot reattach the domain and GitHub reports "The custom domain is already taken".

I am the domain owner and have added the required DNS TXT verification record.
Please release the orphaned Pages domain from my account so I can reuse it.

GitHub typically resolves this within **24 hours**, often sooner.

---

After GitHub releases the domain

Once released, the existing configuration will function immediately:

* TXT record ✅
* A records ✅
* CNAME ✅
* HTTPS provisioning ✅

---

Bottom line

All required steps were completed correctly.
This is a **GitHub Pages domain lock issue**, not a configuration error.

📌 **Next action**
👉 Open [https://github.com/settings/pages/domains](https://github.com/settings/pages/domains)
👉 Confirm whether the domain is listed or absent, then proceed accordingly.


If you want this rewritten again for **README.md**, **internal documentation**, or **plain email format**, I can do that with the same wording.


# **9. Quick Cheat-Sheet and summary of the Guide**

## Standard update

``` bash
quarto render
git add .
git commit -m "Update website"
git push
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Full rebuild

``` bash
git rm -r .
git add -A
git commit -m "Full clean rebuild"
git push
```

Copy new files → push again.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Add one file

``` bash
git add file.qmd
git commit -m "Add new page"
git push
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Delete one file

``` bash
git rm file.qmd
git commit -m "Delete file"
git push
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Exclude large file

``` bash
echo "path/to/file" >> .gitignore
git rm --cached path/to/file
git commit -m "Remove large file"
git push
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Use Git LFS

``` bash
git lfs install
git lfs track "<folder>/*"
git add .gitattributes
git add .
git push
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Clean history

``` bash
git filter-repo --force --path "<file>" --invert-paths
git remote add origin <URL>
git push --force
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

-   Large files should be excluded or moved to LFS

# **10. Troubleshooting Appendix**

This appendix provides a **quick diagnostic guide** for common Git, GitHub Pages, and deployment issues.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.1 Wrong Folder / Git Touching Other System Files**

**Symptom (very dangerous):**

`git status` shows:

```         
AppData/
Documents/
Pictures/
NTUSER.DAT
```

➡️ **You are in the wrong folder (e.g., C:/Users/User)** Git may capture personal system folders.

**Fix:**

1.  Leave folder:

    ``` bash
    cd ~
    ```

2.  Go to correct website repo:

    ``` bash
    cd C:/Users/User/habtamubizuayehu.github.io
    ```

3.  Verify:

    ``` bash
    pwd
    ls -al
    ```

Correct output must show only your website files.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.2 index.lock Error**

**Symptom:**

```         
fatal: Unable to create '.git/index.lock': File exists.
```

**Fix:**

``` bash
rm -f .git/index.lock
```

Then retry your Git command.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.3 Cannot Push — “fetch first” Error**

**Symptom:**

```         
Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have locally.
```

**Fix (safe):**

``` bash
git pull origin main --rebase
git push origin main
```

**Fix (replacing entire site):**

``` bash
git push origin main --force
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.4 GitHub Pages Not Updating**

Checklist:

-   Did you push to **main**?

-   Did your output go to `docs/`?

-   Check Pages logs: <https://github.com/HabtamuBizuayehu/habtamubizuayehu.github.io/actions>

-   TLS Certificate requires **5–30 minutes** If waiting:

    > *Enforce HTTPS — Not yet available*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.5 Website Shows Old Version / Blank Page**

Try:

-   Hard refresh: `Ctrl + Shift + R`
-   Mobile devices: open in private tab
-   Confirm domain maps to GitHub Pages: <https://dnschecker.org>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.6 Push Rejected — File \>100MB**

**Symptom:**

```         
File is 163MB; exceeds GitHub file size limit.
```

**Fix Option A (recommended): remove file & ignore)**

``` bash
git rm --cached <path>
echo "<path>" >> .gitignore
git add .
git commit -m "Remove large file"
git push
```

**Fix Option B (if file exists deep in history):**

``` bash
git filter-repo --force --path "<path>" --invert-paths
git remote add origin https://github.com/HabtamuBizuayehu/habtamubizuayehu.github.io
git push --force
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.7 “origin does not appear to be a git repository”**

Cause: `git filter-repo` removes remote.

Fix:

``` bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/HabtamuBizuayehu/habtamubizuayehu.github.io
git remote -v
```

Then:

``` bash
git push origin main --force
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.8 GitHub Pages: TLS Certificate Pending**

Symptom:

```         
Enforce HTTPS — Not yet available
```

Fix:

-   Wait 5–30 minutes

-   If still pending:

    1.  Remove custom domain
    2.  Re-add
    3.  Save GitHub regenerates certificate

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.9 “Task was canceled” in Pages build**

Cause:

-   Multiple builds triggered at same time
-   Large push with LFS
-   Temporary GitHub Pages congestion

Fix:

-   Do **one** push
-   Wait 2–5 minutes
-   Refresh Actions log

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.10 LFS File Not Displaying on Website**

GitHub Pages **cannot** serve LFS files.

Solution:

-   Link to the raw file on GitHub
-   OR remove from website project
-   OR reduce size and commit without LFS

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.11 Pages Builds Successfully but Site Still Empty**

Checklist:

1.  Does your folder contain `docs/index.html`?

2.  Did you remove all files accidentally?

3.  Run locally:

    ``` bash
    quarto preview
    ```

4.  Confirm GitHub Pages settings:

    -   Branch: `main`
    -   Folder: `/docs`

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.12 “Repository Not Empty” When Cloning**

Symptom:

```         
fatal: destination path exists and is not empty
```

Fix:

Option A — Remove folder manually Option B — Rename:

``` bash
git clone <repo> new_folder
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## **10.13 GitHub Pages Shows Folder Instead of Website**

Cause: No `index.html`.

Fix:

-   Add a home page:

    ``` bash
    quarto render
    git add docs/index.html
    git commit -m "Add homepage"
    git push
    ```
